Goal
* It's difficult to understand the task without first explaining the context. Please rewrite this section as follows:

You are given a minimum-change table. For every amount (index) [[v]], the table tells you which coin to take first when making amount [[v]] using the minimum possible number of coins, or {{-1}} if it is impossible.

<<How to follow the table>>

1. Start with the given target [[amount]].

2. Look up the coin at index [[amount]] (0-based index) in the table and take that coin.

3. Subtract the coin from [[amount]].

4. Go back to Step 2 and repeat until [[amount]] becomes {{0}}.

<<Task>>

Your task is to follow the table from the given target [[amount]] down to {{0}} and output one of the following:

• If the given target [[amount]] is 0, output {{NONE}}.

• If it is possible to make the target [[amount]], output the coins in the order they are taken.

• If the table contains {{-1}} for the amount at any step, output {{IMPOSSIBLE}}.

* Consider adding a worked example at the end of the Goal section. It should be the same as Test 1 (which should be revised as described below).

Input
* Line 1: Please add "space-separated" after "Two".

* Line 2: Please mention explicitly that this line contains the minimum-change table.

Cases
* *Without* modifying the input of the current cases, please either add a new pair of cases or reorder an existing pair so that Test/Validator 1 is a simple case where the output contains different coin values rather than the same coin appearing multiple times. Having identical coins in the output makes the traversal less easy to visualise and understand.

* Please add a new pair of cases where [[amount]] ≠ [[n]] - 1, and the output contains around 10 coins, with only some of those coins having the same value.

Thanks.

Updated the Goal with the table context, numbered traversal steps, explicit output rules, and a worked example matching Test 1 (7 -> 2 -> 0, output 5 2). I also added "space-separated" to Input line 1 and explicitly identified the minimum-change table in line 2.

I moved the existing "Use the stored tie choice" pair to the first position, preserving all existing inputs and outputs. The new "Ten mixed coins with extra entries" pair uses amount/n = 91/97 and 92/100. Each output contains exactly 10 coins with three distinct values and partial repetition.

The C reference solution passed all 10 tests and 10 validators locally. I also independently checked that every table entry satisfies the minimum-coin guarantee.
